detail.abstract: The financial crisis of 2007-08, which is considered the second most severe after the great depression of the 1930s, has affected world economies through the trade and financial channels. According to literature, compared to past global crisis experiences, the 2007-08 economic crisis was severe due to its open economic setup and that can have an impact on the market structure. Hence, this paper examines the restructuring in the market concentration of manufacturing sector in India with respect to the crisis. The study considered 23 manufacturing industries in India for the period from 1991 to 2018. The analysis is based on the PROWESSIQ database (CMIE) and the study revealed that market concentration has increased among 46 percent of Indian manufacturing industries in post crisis period and the crisis variable is positively associated with market concentration with a statistical significance.

title: Role in Behavioral Finance in Investment Decision-Making

detail.title: Role in Behavioral Finance in Investment Decision-Making
detail.abstract:
This study examines how behavioral biases influence the investment decisions of individual investors, particularly young investors. While traditional finance assumes that investors act rationally, real-life decisions are often shaped by emotions, social influence, and psychological tendencies.

The study is based on 171 responses collected through a structured Google Form questionnaire from individuals of different age groups, income levels, occupations, and investment experience. The majority of respondents belong to the “Below 20” and “20–25” age groups and are mostly students with no income and limited investment experience, indicating that the sample mainly represents young and first-time investors.

The findings show that mutual funds, shares, gold, and fixed deposits are the most preferred investment avenues. Mutual funds are the most popular choice, especially among beginners, due to their perceived safety and simplicity. Gold and fixed deposits reflect conservative investment preferences, while shares are chosen by respondents with some income or experience, indicating higher risk-taking ability.

The study concludes that behavioral biases such as herd behavior, risk aversion, familiarity bias, and overconfidence significantly influence investment decisions. However, since the sample is largely dominated by young individuals, the findings may not be fully generalizable to all investor groups.

title: What Makes a Good Rubric? A Quality Framework and Diagnostic Analysis
affiliations: University of Glasgow - Adam Smith Business School

detail.title: What Makes a Good Rubric? A Quality Framework and Diagnostic Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a framework for evaluating and improving rubric design in higher education. It draws on empirical and theoretical literature to develop a systematic instrument for assessing rubric quality, together with practical guidance for implementation. The paper makes two main contributions. First, it introduces a 12-criterion Rubric Quality Framework organised into four dimensions: Rubric Structure, Criteria Design, Performance Descriptors, and Language and Equity. Second, the framework is applied to 79 publicly available rubrics in higher education. The diagnostic analysis shows that moderate to high design quality is common, but the criteria least frequently satisfied concern stating an explicit aggregation rule, framing descriptors in positive and actionable language, and distinguishing performance levels qualitatively rather than by adverbial intensifiers. A practitioner-oriented implementation guide organised across three stages (pre-assessment, assessment period, and post-assessment) complements the analysis with actionable guidance for educators. Taken together, the paper argues that improving rubric design and improving rubric use are related but distinct challenges.

title: CreditSentinel V2: A Hybrid Ensemble Architecture for Institutional Credit Risk
affiliations: NMIMS Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management & Engineering

detail.title: CreditSentinel V2: A Hybrid Ensemble Architecture for Institutional Credit Risk
detail.abstract: The traditional institutional credit risk models predominantly rely on static, historically constrained data sets, which fail to effectively address the issue of real-time market decay and/or localized governance risks. This study, introduces a novel dynamic, hybrid machine learning framework termed CreditSentinel V2 that effectively evaluates corporate solvency through the ingestion of real-time market data. In light of the severe lack of open-source Indian insolvency data sets post the Insolvency Bankruptcy Code of 2016, the framework utilizes the Taiwan Economic Journal bankruptcy data set. This data set is used to train a Tri-Model Ensemble of Extreme Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression algorithms with the aim of effectively mapping the universal mathematical topologies of corporate failure. To effectively train the foreigntrained models on the Indian context, a deterministic Graduated Penalty Mechanism (GPM) is proposed as a layer on top of the Tri-Model Ensemble, effectively stress-testing the localized governance risks. Furthermore, the framework is operationalized through a real-time parsing engine that ingests real-time SEC/NSE filings through financial APIs, effectively leading to a continuous, multi-tiered adjudication framework. In terms of empirical evaluation, the framework is evaluated on the Nifty 500 index, effectively demonstrating the benefits of incorporating non-linear machine learning-based proxies with traditional institutional credit risk rules leading to a highly scalable, fault-tolerant framework.

title: Rational Superstition: Environmental Volatility and the Origins of Magical Beliefs

detail.title: Rational Superstition: Environmental Volatility and the Origins of Magical Beliefs
detail.abstract: This paper provides a global quantitative test of the 'Malinowski Hypothesis,' arguing that uncertainty drives the cultural evolution of magic. We construct a Magical Intensity Index by applying NLP and LLM classification to the Folklore database, covering 1,219 traditional societies. Using daily weather volatility and medieval paleoclimate reconstructions (1100–1400 AD), we find a robust positive relationship: agricultural societies facing higher precipitation variance, droughts, and floods exhibit significantly more magical folklore. To address the endogeneity of agricultural dependence, we instrument for subsistence strategy with crop suitability. Consistent with a risk coping mechanism, the effect is absent for love magic, amplified by soil texture, and mitigated by irrigation or state centralization. An epidemiological analysis of migrants reveals that agricultural magic tracks current local volatility rather than ancestral conditions, suggesting that superstition serves as a functional institutional response to risk. This framework helps explain why non-evidential beliefs remain resilient features of human culture during periods of heightened insecurity.

title: A Quantitative Model of Non-Marriage and Fertility: Bargaining over Leisure

detail.title: A Quantitative Model of Non-Marriage and Fertility: Bargaining over Leisure

declarations.funderStatement: I acknowledge financial support from the Maria de Maeztu Unit of Excellence CEMFI MDM-2016-0684, funded by MCIN/AEI/10.13039/501100011033 and CEMFI.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a new factor contributing to the decline in marriage and fertility: the growth of leisure technology. Over recent decades, high-income countries have experienced two notable shifts in household and family dynamics. First, there has been a significant decline in marriage rates and fertility. Second, time has increasingly been allocated to leisure activities. This paper presents a unified model of marriage and fertility, incorporating intra-household bargaining dynamics. The model, calibrated using data from Japan between 2018 and 2022, is employed to assess the impact of leisure technology growth on marriage and fertility during 2005-2009. The findings highlight that leisure technology growth makes single life relatively more appealing compared to marriage and parenthood. The model explains 22.0% of the decline in marriage and 65.8% of the decrease in fertility.

title: Time-frequency Connectedness Between the ESG Global Indices and GCC Equity Markets: Policy Implications Using the TVP-VAR model
affiliations: Final International University, Final International University and Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK)

detail.title: Time-frequency Connectedness Between the ESG Global Indices and GCC Equity Markets: Policy Implications Using the TVP-VAR model
detail.abstract:
Purpose-This study aims to explore the dynamic connectedness between environmental, social and governance (ESG) global indices and the equity markets of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. The research addresses a gap in understanding how ESG-related shocks propagate through the GCC financial systems, offering valuable insights for investors and policymakers navigating the region's sustainability and market integration agenda. 

Design/methodology/approach-This study uses a time-varying parameter vector autoregressive (TVP-VAR) model integrated with a frequency connectedness framework. It uses daily data from 2014 to 2024, covering the S&P 500 Index, S&P Global 1200 ESG Index, S&P Green Bond Index, S&P Global Clean Energy Index, alongside equity markets from six GCC countries; the inclusion of the S&P 500 Index as a benchmark. This approach allows for the decomposition of volatility transmission across short-and long-term horizons, capturing the evolution of market interactions over time and across frequency bands. 

Findings-The empirical results reveal significant short-term volatility spillovers from global ESG indices to GCC equity markets, particularly during systemic events such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The S&P 500 index and ESG indices are identified as dominant net transmitters of volatility, while Saudi Arabia and the UAE serve as key regional transmitters. In contrast, markets like Kuwait and Bahrain act as net receivers. Long-term spillovers, although less intense, indicate the gradual influence of green finance instruments such as the Green Bond and Clean Energy indices. 

Originality/value-This is among the first studies to apply TVP-VAR in examining ESG-GCC equity market connectedness. It highlights how ESG-driven volatility shapes short-and long-term investment dynamics in resource-based emerging markets.

title: An Event Study of Abnormal Returns and Volatility Patterns in India's NIFTY Financial Services Index Around Union Budget and RBI Monetary Policy Committee Announcements (FY2026)

detail.title: An Event Study of Abnormal Returns and Volatility Patterns in India's NIFTY Financial Services Index Around Union Budget and RBI Monetary Policy Committee Announcements (FY2026)
detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the impact of key macroeconomic and fiscal policy announcements on the NIFTY Financial Services Index during the financial year FY26. The NIFTY Financial Services Index is a sectoral benchmark maintained by NSE Indices Limited, tracking the 20 largest financial services companies listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) of India by free-float market capitalisation. This concentrated composition makes the index highly sensitive to fiscal and monetary policy signals, any change in interest rates, credit regulation, or taxation directly effects the core business economics of its constituents. 

Utilising an event study methodology, the research analyses abnormal returns (AR), cumulative abnormal returns (CAR), and rolling volatility patterns around six key policy events spanning March 31, 2025 to March 31, 2026 including RBI Monetary Policy Committee decisions and the Union Budget presentation. 

Using 247 trading days of daily OHLCV data and a mean adjusted normal return model with a 30 day estimation window and an 11 day event window, we find statistically meaningful evidence of event driven price dislocations. The Union Budget 2026 generated the most severe single day shock with an AR of-2.264% accompanied by a near tripling of post event volatility (Δσ = +1.253%). The Patell Test 2 statistic for this event (t2 =-4.159. p = 0.0003) is the only result reaching the 1% significance threshold in the study.

title: Virtual Power Plant Enhanced Load Restoration in Distribution Networks based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: State Grid Anhui Electric Power Co Ltd, State Grid Anhui Electric Power Co Ltd, State Grid Anhui Electric Power Co Ltd, State Grid Anhui Electric Power Co Ltd, State Grid Anhui Electric Power Co Ltd and Anhui University

detail.title: Virtual Power Plant Enhanced Load Restoration in Distribution Networks based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: Distribution networks may experience faults and blackouts due to various factors, resulting in the isolation of network sections from upstream substations. Conventional distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) relies solely on topological reconnection; even after establishing an optimal radial topology, DNR may still fail to restore loads due to insufficient local power supply capacity. Virtual power plants (VPPs), which aggregate distributed energy resources into a dispatchable entity, provide a complementary way to energize these topologically connected but power-deficient regions. However, integrating VPP coordination into scalable multi-agent reinforcement learning (MADRL) frameworks—while ensuring cross-region collaboration and avoiding action space explosion—remains a critical challenge.This paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach for the joint optimization of network reconfiguration and VPP dispatch. A shared control strategy for critical tie-lines and VPP interconnection switches facilitates cross-community power delivery, while a dynamic action masking mechanism focuses agent learning on fault-affected zones. Evaluated on a real-world 80-node Chinese distribution network where conventional DNR yields limited restoration performance, comparative experiments against state-of-the-art MADRL and DNR-only methods demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves load recovery rate and system operational efficiency.

title: Urban Citizenship In Practice: Everyday Participation Within Turkish Student Associations In Milan

detail.title: Urban Citizenship In Practice: Everyday Participation Within Turkish Student Associations In Milan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: All participants provided informed consent prior to the interviews. Data were anonymized and used exclusively for academic purposes.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This thesis examines how Turkish university students in Milan enact participation and agency through their involvement in student associations. Drawing on urban citizenship as an analytical framework, the study conceptualizes participation as practice-based and embedded in everyday organizational life within the urban context of Milan. The analysis is based on thirteen semi-structured interviews conducted with members of Turkish student associations operating at both city-wide and university-based levels in Milan. Through a qualitative and interpretive approach, the study investigates how participation is shaped by student status, migration-related conditions, temporariness, and informal organizational arrangements within the urban context. The findings show that participation enacted through relational and pragmatic practices such as mutual support, coordination of activities, and navigation of institutional environments. Agency appears uneven and situational, expanding and contracting in response to academic pressures, organizational demands, and structural constraints. Informality functions both as an enabling condition for participation and as a source of differentiated capacities to act within associations. By foregrounding everyday organizational practices within the specific context of Milan, the thesis refines practice-oriented approaches to urban citizenship by demonstrating how maintenance and mediation, rather than rupture or claims-making, structure participation under conditions of temporariness and institutional constraint. These practices are closely tied to the spatial, institutional, and economic organization of Milan as a metropolitan university city.

title: Mortgage Burnout and Selection Effects in Heterogeneous Cox Hazard Models

detail.title: Mortgage Burnout and Selection Effects in Heterogeneous Cox Hazard Models
detail.abstract: We study the aggregate hazard rate of a heterogeneous population whose individual event intensities are modeled as Cox (doubly stochastic) processes. In the deterministic hazard setting, the observed pool hazard is the survival weighted mean of the individual hazards, and its time derivative equals the mean individual hazard drift minus a variance term. This yields a transparent structural explanation of burnout in mortgage pools. We extend this perspective to stochastic intensity models. The observed pool hazard remains a survival-weighted mean, but now evolves as an Ito process whose drift contains the mean drift of the individual hazards and a negative selection term driven by cross-sectional dispersion, together with a diffusion term inherited from the common factor. We formulate the general identity and discuss special cases relevant to mortgage prepayment modeling.

title: The Conglomerate Power Puzzle

detail.title: The Conglomerate Power Puzzle
detail.abstract: The modern U.S. economy presents a surprisingly open puzzle that standard antitrust concepts struggle to explain. At the macro level of entire sectors, a small number of firms increasingly dominate broad sectors and profits have surged. Simultaneously, at the micro level of individual products, concentration appears largely stable. I call this divergence between micro-and the macro-measures of concentration the Conglomerate Power Puzzle. This Article presents the first comprehensive resolution to this puzzle. It argues that firms increasingly grow not by monopolizing a single market, but by acquiring businesses in adjacent products and services-transactions that often fall outside traditional antitrust screens. I label this the Adjacent Market Takeover strategy. Because U.S. antitrust enforcers review proposed mergers largely by focusing on mergers' effects at the level of individual product markets at the micro level, they may systematically miss acquisitions whose competitive significance emerges only when ownership is aggregated across different markets at the macro level. The Article identifies three overlooked channels of harm from Adjacent Market Takeovers and explains why current merger review often misses them. Four case studies in pharmaceuticals and healthcare show how Adjacent Market Takeovers can explain the Conglomerate Power Puzzle in practice and how firms can build cross-market power with limited public and regulatory scrutiny. The Article concludes that the United States faces a conglomerate enforcement gap, one that extends beyond pharmaceuticals and healthcare to any industry where firms can accumulate that power through adjacent acquisitions while evading traditional antitrust review.

detail.abstract: Europe still relies heavily on non-European card rails for domestic payments. I assemble a 32-country dataset from central bank and industry sources and use conservative fee assumptions on purpose, to avoid overstating the cost case where country inputs are uneven. Even on that basis, the model indicates about EUR 17.9 billion in yearly merchant acceptance costs, with EUR 13.4 billion linked to Visa/Mastercard-dominated rails. The key uncertainty is whether interoperability and governance choices can align incentives for broad merchant acceptance without recreating comparable fee extraction under a new label.

title: Timelink: Time-Aware Record Linkage With Semi-Markov Dynamics

detail.title: Timelink: Time-Aware Record Linkage With Semi-Markov Dynamics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses only publicly available, de-identified government data (North Carolina voter registration snapshots, IPUMS historical census samples from 1900 and 1920) and synthetic simulation data. No primary data collection from human subjects was conducted. No IRB approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Record linkage-determining whether records in different databases refer to the same person-is foundational to health research, official statistics, and public administration. The classical Fellegi-Sunter (FS) framework treats all field comparisons as static, ignoring that attributes like address and marital status change over time. We propose TimeLink, a semi-Markov extension of FS that classifies fields as stable (time-invariant), dynamic (low-cardinality, modeled via semi-Markov transition matrices), or semi-stable (high-cardinality, modeled via Weibull survival times). Match weights are derived from a coherent generative model, depend on the time gap, and reduce to a standard FS additive score with precomputed weights. On North Carolina voter registration data (10-year gap), TimeLink achieves F1 = 0.877 vs. 0.751 for classical FS; on IPUMS historical census records (20year gap), F1 = 0.668 vs. 0.146; and in a controlled simulation spanning 10-30 year gaps, classical FS collapses to F1 = 0.055 while TimeLink maintains F1 above 0.85, matching supervised methods without labeled data. TimeLink thus enables accurate unsupervised linkage across decade-scale gaps where classical methods fail.

title: Closing the DORA Gap: A Three-Tier Architecture for Cyber Incident Disclosure

detail.title: Closing the DORA Gap: A Three-Tier Architecture for Cyber Incident Disclosure
detail.abstract:
The European Union’s Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) is the most advanced mandatory cyber incident reporting regime currently in force for the financial sector. It has two structural gaps: no confidential non-punitive learning channel (Tier 1) and no mechanism for principled management of public disclosure decisions (Tier 3). These gaps are not incidental omissions. They follow from a single design error – conflating learning and deterrence within a single attributable reporting channel – that creates rational incentives to minimise governance-failure documentation at precisely the point where candid documentation matters most.

This article proposes a three-tier disclosure architecture that closes both gaps. Tier 1 is a confidential, non-punitive learning channel administered by ENISA with statutory information barriers against enforcement authority access. Tier 2 is the existing DORA framework, formalised and structurally separated from Tier 1. Tier 3 is a structured public disclosure requirement with a mandatory suppression-rationale declaration that makes principled suppression decisions visible and auditable without eliminating them where genuinely justified.

The article presents a concrete implementation pathway through DORA’s Article 20 delegated act mechanism and five specific recommendations for ENISA, the European Commission, and national competent authorities. The collective action and comparative theoretical foundations underpinning the proposal are developed in a companion academic analysis; this article focuses on the architectural design and regulatory implementation.

title: Data Centers and the Ethical Dilemma of AI: A Project Management Framework for Responsible Infrastructure Governance

detail.title: Data Centers and the Ethical Dilemma of AI: A Project Management Framework for Responsible Infrastructure Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, or institutional conflicts of interest related to this work. The views expressed are solely those of the author as an independent researcher.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual framework and literature-based study with no human participants or personally identifiable data, so formal ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant or external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified demand for data centers, concentrating energy, water, and computational resources into a relatively small number of physical sites. While policymakers and industry often describe data centers as neutral technical infrastructure, work in AI ethics, environmental science, and critical infrastructure studies shows that siting, design, and operational choices redistribute environmental burdens and social risks across communities and ecosystems. At the same time, project management standards increasingly acknowledge sustainability but offer limited practical guidance for integrating ethical, environmental, and social criteria into project decisions. This paper proposes the Ethical Infrastructure Assessment Model (EIAM), a project management framework for evaluating proposed data center developments through four analytical pillars: Environmental Stewardship, Community and Social Impact, Transparency and Governance, and Responsible AI Alignment. Each pillar is operationalized into qualitative questions and quantitative indicators that can be scored, weighted, and combined into an overall ethical risk profile, culminating in a Go, Mitigate, or No Go decision. EIAM is designed for project sponsors, owners, and public agencies who must balance industrial growth, grid reliability, local well being, and AI driven innovation. Rather than presenting ethics as an abstract add on, EIAM embeds ethical considerations in project governance, risk registers, and stage gate decisions, providing practitioners with a structured approach to deciding not only whether a data center can be built, but whether it should be built in its proposed form and location.

detail.title: Treasury Supply Shocks: Propagation Through Debt Expansion and Maturity Adjustment

publicationDetails.detailsText: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Working Paper No. RWP 26-04
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Historically high debt-to-GDP levels in the U.S. have raised concerns about future financial market stability and fiscal sustainability. We use high-frequency data and consider Treasury futures price changes within narrow windows around auction announcements in order to identify two distinct Treasury supply shocks: debt volume shocks that capture changes in the level of public debt, and maturity adjustment shocks that reflect changes in the maturity structure. We find that debt expansion shocks raise yields across the curve by increasing term premia, leading to tighter financial conditions. These shocks crowd out private sector activity by reducing investment and production, particularly during periods of rapid debt growth. In contrast, maturity extension shocks steepen the yield curve while lowering credit risk premia and fiscal uncertainty. By reducing risk premia, these shocks stimulate near-term investment and production, even as higher long-term borrowing costs weigh on longer-horizon investment. We also show that the Treasury debt management policy can meaningfully interact with the Federal Reserve's asset purchase programs.

title: The Cluster Panacea? An Evaluation of Three Interventions in Shrimp value Chains in Bangladesh
affiliations: International Food Policy Research Institute, Michigan State University - Department of Agricultural, Food and Resource Economics, , International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) and International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI)

detail.title: The Cluster Panacea? An Evaluation of Three Interventions in Shrimp value Chains in Bangladesh
detail.abstract: Clustering farming has often been proposed as an effective way to overcome the significant transactions costs faced by downstream buyers in interacting and negotiating with many small farmers, while making it easier for extension workers and governments to dispense advice, provide upstream services and inputs. In this study, we evaluate the impact of a set of three initiatives in Bangladesh, implemented by a government department, a private sector processing firm and a not-for-profit industrial advocacy body, all involving clustering contiguous shrimp farm ponds to enable group certification necessary for global market access. We implement a canonical difference-in-differences model using two rounds of surveys of a sample of over 1,222 farmers in 2023 and 2024 to assess the impacts on pond management practices, net profits and any unintended impacts on food security and dietary diversity. Our results suggest that the cluster interventions had impressive impacts on adoption of better farm management practices. However, these do not appear to translate into significant gains in net profits, perhaps because these interventions are still relatively new. Further, it appears that cluster farmers pay a penalty on account of a shift to more intensive cultivation, represented by a loss in species diversity and lower incomes from fish and vegetables. We find that there are no significant spillover effects as yet on shrimp farmers in the same village as the clusters. This study reflects critically on the efficacy of clustering that is presumed to enhance access to global markets.

title: Misconceptions About AI in Decision Systems: Signal, Execution, and Governance

detail.title: Misconceptions About AI in Decision Systems: Signal, Execution, and Governance
detail.abstract: Public discussion about artificial intelligence often treats failure as a property of the model alone. This paper argues that many failures in AI-enabled decision settings originate earlier, at the level of conceptual framing: institutions collapse model capability, system behavior, and governance into a single expectation. Once AI is imagined as a tool, a search engine, or an autonomous substitute for judgment, organizations misread what the model produces and where responsibility sits. The paper offers a compact taxonomy of misconceptions at the model, system, governance, and social levels; shows how they distort implementation; and links them to the distinction between signal and execution. The note is exploratory and intended as a framework for empirical extension rather than as a final theory of AI failure.

title: Assessing the Impact of Rice Price Stabilization Policies in Bangladesh: Results from a Stochastic Spatial Equilibrium Model
affiliations: International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), , , International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) and International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI)

detail.title: Assessing the Impact of Rice Price Stabilization Policies in Bangladesh: Results from a Stochastic Spatial Equilibrium Model
detail.abstract:
Rice plays a central role in the diet in Bangladesh and as a source of income for farmers. Although Bangladesh has largely liberalized international trade in rice, it maintains a public food distribution system to stabilize prices, distributing an average of 2 million tons of rice per year at a cost of almost US$ 800 million per year. This study explores whether alternative policies could achieve similar stabilization at a lower cost. It uses a stochastic spatial-equilibrium model of rice markets to simulate monthly prices in eight regions of the country. Stochastic shocks are used to simulate fluctuations in regional production, replicating historical patterns at the region-season level, as well as inter-regional correlation in production shocks. It also simulates fluctuation in world rice prices, mimicking the mean, variance, and serial correlation of historical wholesale prices of rice in Delhi. Public procurement and distribution follow historic averages by month and region. Private storage is represented by a simplified version of rational expectations models, in which net storage is a non-linear function of availability in the previous month.

One set of simulations tests alternative levels of distribution, finding that cutting distribution to 1 million tons would have minimal effects on the level of rice price stability. Another set of simulations tested different import tariff levels, including the baseline rate of 25%1. We find that lower tariffs result in both lower rice prices and less price instability, as world rice prices tend to be more stable than local prices. Simulating a buffer stock with different price bands shows that a narrow band can achieve high price stability but at a high fiscal cost. A 20 T/kg (USD 0.26/kg) price band generates similar price stabilization at a lower cost compared to current policy. However, it is difficult to set the “right” purchase and sale price, and many simulations result in exhausting reserves or reaching warehouse capacity. An adaptive buffer stock, in which the price is adjusted as the stock runs too low or too high, solves some of these problems. In general, the study finds that current procurement and distribution patterns do not match well with the regional and monthly patterns of surplus and deficit, possibly reflecting multiple and conflicting goals of the public food distribution system.

title: The Synchronized Departure Equilibrium: A Unified Model of Asymmetric Crowd and Traffic Flow with Applications to Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure, Digital Platforms, and Event Management

detail.title: The Synchronized Departure Equilibrium: A Unified Model of Asymmetric Crowd and Traffic Flow with Applications to Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure, Digital Platforms, and Event Management
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Synchronized Departure Equilibrium (SDE), a formal model for systems in which distributed user arrivals are followed by a near-simultaneous mass service request triggered by a shared synchronizing event-a phenomenon that dominates modern AI inference infrastructure, content delivery networks, and web API overloads. The canonical digital example is an AI model launch: millions of users arrive at a service independently over hours, but a single public announcement triggers a near-simultaneous burst of inference requests that overwhelms full-precision GPU endpoints. We formalize three original contributions. First, the Synchronization Index S ∈ [0, 1], a continuous parameter quantifying the fraction of total traffic arriving in an instantaneous burst at the synchronization trigger time T*-a primitive absent from existing queuing, traffic, or distributed systems models. Second, a Heterogeneous Threshold Equilibrium in which users with heterogeneous quality-sensitivity costs self-sort between premium capacity (full-precision GPU inference, origin servers) and degraded capacity (INT4-quantized models, CDN edge cache), producing a time-varying threshold θ*(t) structurally distinct from the Wardrop User Equilibrium (1952) due to the permanent exclusion of SLA-bound enterprise clients who cannot accept quantized responses at any queue length. Third, the Infrastructure Sizing Theorem with complete proof: the welfare-optimal budget share allocated to premium infrastructure, α*(S), is strictly decreasing and convex in S, with exact closed-form solution α*(S) = δρ / [S√(ρ-1) + δ(ρ-1)], where ρ = C_p/C_d is the premium-to-degraded cost multiplier and δ is the captive SLA constituency fraction. We apply the SDE framework across eight domains-AI inference, CDN traffic management, internet flash crowds, financial market microstructure, government digital portals, physical event venues, urban transport nodes, and municipal building infrastructure-with digital and AI systems given analytical priority. A physical analogy (building egress observed at a 2,000-person Mumbai event) is used to ground the abstract digital routing mechanics but is secondary to the primary digital contributions. Policy implications for AI infrastructure procurement, CDN architecture, and smart city digital infrastructure are discussed.

title: Leveraging the Kaizen Methodology To Build Digital Skills in India Through Multistakeholder Partnerships

detail.title: Leveraging the Kaizen Methodology To Build Digital Skills in India Through Multistakeholder Partnerships
detail.abstract: India's rapidly expanding workforce faces a growing digital skills gap, with millions expected to require reskilling in AI and emerging technologies over the next decade. Addressing this at scale demands not just ambition but operational precision, particularly when delivery depends on complex multistakeholder partnerships spanning government, industry, and implementation partners. This white paper examines how the kaizen methodology was applied within such a partnership to continuously improve program design and delivery, ultimately enhancing both the effectiveness and efficiency of a national AI skilling initiative in India. Through three core kaizen tools, namely rose bud thorn design thinking, process gap analysis, and incident management with corrective action planning, the steering committee was able to systematically identify friction points, streamline learner registration, and resolve structural program issues in real time. The paper argues that kaizen offers a practical and adaptable framework for multi-stakeholder partnerships seeking to improve coordination, reduce operational waste, and maximise social impact at scale.

title: Examination of the Emergence and Development of the Philosophy of Education in the Qom Seminary Over the Last Century
affiliations: and Research Institute of Hawzah and University

detail.title: Examination of the Emergence and Development of the Philosophy of Education in the Qom Seminary Over the Last Century
detail.abstract: Introduction and Objectives: Throughout history, Islamic seminaries (ḥawzah) have consistently undertaken the mission of promoting religion, ethics, spirituality, and the education of society, adapting their efforts to the conditions and available resources of each era. These seminaries trained the necessary human resources—including teachers, preachers, Imams of congregational prayers and Friday prayers—and through the establishment of schools and maktab-khānahs, contributed directly to the education of the public. A brief historical review shows that, in addition to educational activities, seminaries have played a pioneering role in research and knowledge production in the field of education, generating works on moral education, the ethics of teaching and learning, educational methods, and related topics. Since its reestablishment by Ḥājj Shaykh ʿAbd al-Karīm Ḥāʾerī, the Qom Seminary has paid serious attention to education and upbringing, acting in both theoretical and practical capacities. The aim of this article is to examine, from a historical perspective, the role of the Qom Seminary in shaping and developing the philosophy of education during the last cetury. The fundamental question addressed here is: What role has the Qom Seminary played over the last century in the emergence of the philosophy of education as an academic field, and through what developments has this process unfolded? Methodology: This study employs a historical–analytical method. Using documentary and library data, it investigates the emergence, evolution, and deepening of the philosophy of education in the Qom Seminary over the last cetury. By analyzing historical trends, official documents, published works from seminary, and institutional developments—such as the establishment of the Office for Seminary–University Cooperation—the theoretical and institutional trajectory of this development is reconstructed. The main focus is the analysis of scientific texts, policy documents, and major scholarly works from each historical period, in order to provide a systematic and comparative account of the growth of philosophy of education within this academic institution.

title: The Perception Gap: How World Models Will Eliminate the Human-Mediated Input Layer in Enterprise Software

detail.title: The Perception Gap: How World Models Will Eliminate the Human-Mediated Input Layer in Enterprise Software
detail.abstract: Enterprise software encodes a five-decade structural assumption: human beings are the perception layer between the physical world and digital systems. This paper argues that this assumption-not any particular product feature-is the foundational architectural premise of an entire class of software, and that world models capable of directly perceiving physical environments will eliminate it. We introduce the Enterprise Software Perception Dependency Spectrum (EPDS), a framework classifying enterprise software by dependence on human perception as a primary input mechanism. Using Salesforce and Microsoft as representative cases, we map 22 product lines across three EPDS classes. We analyze how Meta's V-JEPA 2-achieving zero-shot robot planning from under 62 hours of unlabeled video-demonstrates that the perception layer is approaching enterprise viability. Finally, we propose the Business OS, a three-layer transitional architecture grounded in sociotechnical systems theory. Disruption will be asymmetric: vendors whose revenue concentrates in perception-dependent categories face elimination-level exposure, while digitally-native vendors are positioned to own the agent and governance layers of the emerging architecture.

title: Generative AI and Firm Hiring Demand: Evidence from Advanced and Developing Economies

detail.title: Generative AI and Firm Hiring Demand: Evidence from Advanced and Developing Economies
detail.abstract: We study how the release of ChatGPT in November 2022 affected firm hiring demand across 186 countries, using 77.8 million online job postings from 37,395 firmcountry pairs over 2021Q2-2025Q3. We construct predetermined firm-country AI exposure from 2019 occupational composition and estimate a continuous difference-in-differences design. The results reveal a divergent global adjustment. In advanced economies, posting volumes decline gradually beginning three to four quarters after ChatGPT's release, with compositional shifts toward fewer high-substitution vacancies emerging later. In developing economies, posting volumes begin to decline earlier in the event window, with compositional changes following by the third quarter. In both groups, more exposed firms reduce the share of high-substitution postings and lower the posting-weighted AI substitution mix, but the adjustment is faster and more front-loaded in developing economies. These patterns are consistent with generative AI reshaping hiring demand differently across development groups, with developing economies adjusting earlier and with clearer evidence on the composition margin than on overall posting volumes.

title: Bias, Judgment, and Decision-Making in Modern Organizations: A CFO's Perspective

detail.title: Bias, Judgment, and Decision-Making in Modern Organizations: A CFO's Perspective

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This paper reflects independent research and professional experience.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or primary data collection. Any case illustrations are derived from professional experience and have been fully anonymized to protect confidentiality and privacy.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Decision-making in modern organizations is often assumed to be rational, data-driven, and objective. Yet, in practice, strategic choices are frequently shaped by cognitive biases, organizational pressures, and imperfect information. Drawing on over two decades of leadership experience in finance across diverse industries, this paper explores the gap between theoretical rationality and real-world decision-making. It builds on themes explored in Smart But Wrong (Muhammad, 2025), which examines how intelligent organizations arrive at flawed decisions due to biased interpretation of data and misplaced confidence in structured processes. The paper examines how biases manifest in areas such as hiring, strategy formulation, and financial judgment, and highlights the limitations of relying on data without contextual understanding. Through practical case illustrations, it demonstrates how both visible metrics and hidden dynamics shape outcomes. It further explores emerging challenges, including decision fatigue at senior leadership levels and the evolving role of artificial intelligence in influencing organizational choices. The paper argues for a more balanced approach that integrates analytical rigor with human judgment, ethical awareness, and contextual insight.

title: Governing the Social Vacuum: How Vulnerability and Social Norms Shape Prosocial Behavior in Unsupervised Service Environments
affiliations: Wuhan University - Economics and Management School, Arizona State University (ASU) - W.P. Carey School of Business, Arizona State University (ASU) and Wuhan University

detail.title: Governing the Social Vacuum: How Vulnerability and Social Norms Shape Prosocial Behavior in Unsupervised Service Environments
detail.abstract: Robotic agents increasingly operate in unsupervised service environments, yet the resulting "social vacuum" often lowers the threshold for human abuse and neglect. To address this governance challenge, we investigate and compare two distinct behavioral interventions: social norm appeals (reconstructing social constraints) and revealing AI vulnerability (acknowledging a competence gap). Across a largescale randomized field experiment with a leading robotaxi firm operating at scale, and a controlled laboratory experiment, we find that both strategies significantly reduce antisocial behavior (littering). However, our results reveal that they operate through fundamentally different psychological pathways with distinct boundary conditions. Social norm appeals function through a logic of compliance. Field analyses show that this strategy is fragile under environmental stress (e.g., adverse weather), which depletes cognitive resources. Further analyses also suggest that riders exposed to such appeals may exhibit a slight reduction in their willingness to take a subsequent ride. In contrast, revealing AI vulnerability operates through a logic of empowerment; by highlighting the user's unique capacity to help, it awakens prosocial efficacy, remaining robust regardless of external stressors. Our laboratory experiment validates these distinct mechanisms, confirming that social norm appeals operate via descriptive norms while AI vulnerability signals operate via perceived prosocial impact. Finally, we uncover a substitution effect: combining these strategies yields no synergistic benefit in a field setting, suggesting that firms can leverage these distinct psychological levers as a strategic portfolio to effectively manage the social vacuum of automation.

title: Managing Regulatory Enforcement Risk In Employment-Based Immigration: A Systems-Based Governance Framework For Institutional Accountability

detail.title: Managing Regulatory Enforcement Risk In Employment-Based Immigration: A Systems-Based Governance Framework For Institutional Accountability
detail.abstract:
Employment-based immigration in the United States operates within a complex and highly regulated environment that exposes organizations to significant regulatory enforcement risk. Employers sponsoring foreign workers must comply with overlapping requirements enforced by agencies such as the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Department of Labor, and Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Despite the critical importance of compliance, many organizations continue to rely on fragmented, manual processes that increase the likelihood of errors, missed deadlines, and audit exposure. This study addresses this gap by examining how regulatory enforcement risk can be mitigated through a systems-based approach to institutional accountability.

The study adopts a conceptual research design supported by a structured review of interdisciplinary literature spanning regulatory governance, institutional theory, and information systems. Through conceptual synthesis, the study develops an integrated theoretical framework linking regulatory pressures, risk governance mechanisms, and information systems capabilities. Building on this foundation, a systems governance framework is proposed to operationalize compliance as a lifecycle-based, technology-enabled, and continuously monitored process.

title: Managers and the Persistence of Productivity

detail.title: Managers and the Persistence of Productivity
detail.abstract: Standard two-way fixed effects models assume that a manager's effect on performance is fully realized upon assignment. We develop a framework in which plant output depends on a latent managerial stock that depreciates at rate δ and is replenished by the current manager's productivity. We prove that δ is point-identified and that ignoring persistence understates both managerial productivity dispersion and the variance share attributable to managers. Applying our framework to CEO data, we estimate low persistence for profitability (δ ≈ 0.21) but high persistence for firm scale (δ ≈ 0.73 for sales, δ ≈ 0.78 for employment), implying that the standard variance decomposition understates the dispersion of CEO effects on firm scale by 50-60 percent. We then show in two political economy settings that ignoring persistence substantially understates the estimated effects of reforms that change how leaders are selected: the long-run cost of patronage in the British Empire is roughly 4 times the static estimate, and the quality differential from discretionary appointment in Qing China is 2.4 times larger.

title: The End of the Feed: Sovereign Narrative Experience and the Case for AI-Assisted Discovery and Continuation

detail.title: The End of the Feed: Sovereign Narrative Experience and the Case for AI-Assisted Discovery and Continuation
detail.abstract: Recommendation algorithms are structurally incapable of understanding why a person responds to a work of art. They match metadata to metadata: genre tags, viewing history, demographic proxies. They cannot see the thread connecting three apparently unlike things a person loves, because that thread is not a category. It is a ratio of qualities-dread and beauty, formal precision and emotional devastation, the uncanny made domestic. This paper argues that AI-assisted discovery and continuation represents a qualitatively different relationship between a person and their narrative experience. The first claim is that conversational AI can identify aesthetic threads that algorithms cannot, because conversation operates on meaning rather than metadata. The second and more radical claim is that AI may enable sovereign narrative continuation: the extension of stories that were structurally complete but infrastructurally abandoned. Cancelled shows, unfinished mythologies, and truncated narrative arcs are reframed here as medium shocks-coordination failures in the delivery infrastructure, not in the story itself. The ratio that made them resonant can keep running. The instrument for continuing it now exists.

title: Building Audit-Ready Immigration Sponsorship Systems: A Documentation Governance Framework For Employers In Uganda

detail.title: Building Audit-Ready Immigration Sponsorship Systems: A Documentation Governance Framework For Employers In Uganda
detail.abstract: Work permit processing delays and weak audit readiness remain persistent challenges for organizations managing expatriate employees in Uganda. While these challenges are often attributed to external regulatory inefficiencies, this study argues that a significant proportion of delays originate from internal organizational practices, particularly the absence of structured documentation governance systems. This study adopts a conceptual and qualitative approach to examine how fragmented documentation processes, inconsistent record management, and weak accountability mechanisms contribute to compliance gaps and operational inefficiencies in immigration sponsorship. Drawing on Institutional Theory, Documentation Governance Theory, and Information Systems Governance, the study develops a comprehensive framework that reconceptualizes immigration sponsorship as a governance and systems-driven process. The findings reveal that documentation fragmentation, lack of standardization, limited use of compliance tracking tools, and weak escalation mechanisms are key factors undermining both audit readiness and processing efficiency. In response, the study proposes a Documentation Governance System Framework that integrates lifecycle-based process management, compliance matrices, escalation frameworks, and system integration to support structured and proactive compliance. The proposed framework emphasizes practical applicability within the Ugandan context, demonstrating how organizations can leverage existing tools such as spreadsheets, shared drives, and basic digital systems to implement governance mechanisms without requiring extensive technological investment. By improving documentation accuracy, enhancing accountability, and enabling real-time monitoring of compliance activities, the framework offers a scalable solution for reducing processing delays and strengthening audit readiness.

title: Deep-Tech Innovation: A Multi-Method Study toward a Conceptual Framework and Research Agenda
affiliations: University of Münster, , University of Münster, Bern University of Applied Sciences (BFH), University of Münster and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Entrepreneurship Center

detail.abstract: The term "deep-tech innovation" has attracted growing attention in research and practice, but it is applied inconsistently and lacks an agreed-upon definition. This limits cumulative knowledge building and blurs how deep-tech innovation relates to adjacent concepts. We address this gap by developing a framework that treats deep-tech innovation as a distinct object of inquiry. Using a multi-method design that combines a systematic, integrative, conceptcentric literature review and semi-structured interviews with deep-tech founders, we identify twelve defining attributes structured across three levels: invention, venture, and ecosystem. At the invention level (the conceptual core), we specify six attributes: three foundational attributes that capture the scientific and technological basis of the invention (scientific origins, hardware intensity, and an enabling platform character), and three attributes that describe its characteristic exposure profile (long development timelines, high capital intensity, and multilayered uncertainty). The remaining six attributes capture recurring implications at the venture level (staged financing strategies, dual scientific and commercial maturation, and the multidisciplinary broadening of teams) and the ecosystem level (multi-actor interactions, specialized incubation support, and industrial de-risking and scaling partnerships). We use this framework to delineate the boundaries of deep-tech innovation, distinguish it from adjacent concepts, and propose an agenda for future research.

title: From Apparent AI Efficiency to Realized Productivity: Verification Friction in AI-Augmented Knowledge Work

detail.title: From Apparent AI Efficiency to Realized Productivity: Verification Friction in AI-Augmented Knowledge Work
detail.abstract: Generative AI can produce visible gains in speed and performance, but those gains do not translate cleanly into realized productivity in accountable knowledge work. Current productivity studies typically capture aggregate performance outcomes, while research shows that workers often spend additional effort checking, interpreting, and correcting AI output. This paper develops a conceptual bridge across information systems, human–computer interaction, and economics literatures to address this gap. In the underlying mechanism, AI factual unreliability increases cognitive verification load, while LLM literacy shapes how efficiently the burden is managed. The paper introduces verification friction as the episode-level economic cost that arises when the constraint pathway becomes consequential in AI-assisted work. It also develops a measurement bridge for situations where human-with-AI time is recorded as a single on-platform interval. In those cases, apparent gross savings can overstate realized gains because some verification and correction occur outside the recorded interaction. The result is a framework for distinguishing visible AI acceleration from burden-adjusted realized value.

title: AI Washing: How Firms Use Artificial Intelligence Narratives to Mask Offshoring, Recessionary Cost-Cutting, and Post-Pandemic Restructuring

detail.title: AI Washing: How Firms Use Artificial Intelligence Narratives to Mask Offshoring, Recessionary Cost-Cutting, and Post-Pandemic Restructuring

detail.abstract: In 2025, artificial intelligence was cited as the cause in 54,836 layoffs, culminating in Block, Inc.'s February 2026 elimination of approximately 4,000 positions attributed to "intelligence tools." Yet Block's own CEO had explicitly denied AI as a layoff driver eleven months earlier, and the company's headcount reduction returned staffing to pre-pandemic levels that predated any of the cited AI tools. Independent evidence from executive surveys, technology assessments, and legally mandated layoff disclosures consistently finds that the AI capabilities firms cite to investors are not reflected in any other evidence channel. This article argues that AI washing, the strategic practice of attributing workforce reductions to artificial intelligence capabilities that did not cause them, functions as a multi-layered narrative whose documentary traces are consistent with three convergent restructuring forces: offshoring of white-collar positions, recessionary cost-cutting driven by tariffs and credit tightening, and correction of pandemic-era over-hiring. Drawing on institutional theory, signaling theory, and the greenwashing literature, the article develops a Triple Concealment Model identifying these forces and proposes signal quality inversion as a mechanism explaining why capital markets reward unverified AI claims. A documentary analysis across six independent evidence categories provides the empirical foundation. The article offers a five-question diagnostic framework enabling boards, investors, and workforce leaders to distinguish genuine AI transformation from strategic narrative packaging.

title: The Sweet Caroline Invariant: 45 Seconds of Functional Resonance in High-Variance Systems

detail.title: The Sweet Caroline Invariant: 45 Seconds of Functional Resonance in High-Variance Systems
detail.abstract: This paper examines a recurring collective synchronization event observable in large-scale human gatherings: the approximately 45-second window during which a crowd singing Sweet Caroline achieves measurable behavioral coherence. The event is typically credited to the song's cultural popularity or emotional resonance. This paper proposes a different account. The mechanism appears to be structural rather than sentimental: a specific ratio of constraint and variance imposed on a high-noise system, producing brief but reliable collective alignment. The song is not the cause. It is the delivery mechanism for a ratio that the system was already capable of achieving. The distinction matters because it suggests that collective coordination at scale does not require shared belief, shared narrative, or any particular cultural content. It requires a correctly structured anchor. This specimen may be one of the most widely replicated unrecognized demonstrations of the Coordination Invariant (S = C/V) in recorded human behavior.

title: Cartel Persistence as an Equilibrium Outcome of Enforcement Design

detail.title: Cartel Persistence as an Equilibrium Outcome of Enforcement Design
detail.abstract: This article develops an analytical economic framework to explain cartel formation and persistence as equilibrium outcomes of market structure and enforcement design. Rather than treating cartels as isolated legal violations, the framework models collusion as a rational response to concentrated market structures, repeated interaction, and imperfect enforcement technologies. The analysis emphasizes how detection probability, sanction design, and institutional capacity jointly shape firms' incentives to sustain or abandon collusive equilibria. Within this setting, traditional sanction-based deterrence may fail to destabilize cartels when structural conditions favor coordination. The framework yields clear comparative statics regarding the effects of market concentration, transparency, and enforcement credibility on cartel stability. These results generate testable implications for the design of antitrust enforcement, including the role of leniency programs and proactive market screening. By integrating insights from industrial organization and deterrence economics, the article contributes to the law and economics literature on cartel enforcement and institutional design.

title: The Map Inversion: A Shared Puzzle About How We See the World - And What Becomes Possible When We Look From Outside

detail.title: The Map Inversion: A Shared Puzzle About How We See the World - And What Becomes Possible When We Look From Outside
detail.abstract: This paper invites consideration of a structural shift in how human behavioral systems are interpretedmoving from an internal, moral-evaluative map to an external, mechanical lens. By viewing the human instrument as a system regulated by the balance of constraint and variance, recurring patterns of "looping" (blame, guilt, and retrospective rewriting) become visible as predictable systemic noise rather than personal or collective failure. The Coordination Invariant S = C/V (developed across a broader body of work and formalized in the March 2026 capstone "Consciousness as a Ratio") offers one way to see this. The paper introduces the concept of the "Map Inversion"-a move toward participatory objectivity through stable, shared external references. This shift appears to enable forward-moving systemic alignment without the necessity of correcting past states, with possible implications for coordination in interpersonal, organizational, and technological systems.

title: Robust Assortment Optimization With Value Conscious Customers Under Nested Logit Model
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Department of Data and Systems Engineering, The University of Hong Kong and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Robust Assortment Optimization With Value Conscious Customers Under Nested Logit Model
detail.abstract: We study the assortment optimization problem under the nested logit choice model where its estimated utilities of products and estimated dissimilarity factors of nests are uncertain and both lie in rectangular uncertainty sets. Under competitive alternatives and fully captured nests settings, the objective is to find a robust assortment such that the worst-case expected revenue is maximized. We show that, when the estimated utilities satisfy a proposed revenue-utility conscious (RUC) condition (a weaker version of the "value conscious" condition), the robust assortment optimization problem can be transformed into an equivalent tractable linear program with both estimated utilities and dissimilarity factors chosen as their lower bounds. In that case, nested-by-revenue assortment attains optimality. We also demonstrate that the size of the robust assortment grows monotonically as utility uncertainty expands, yet it behaves non-monotonically with respect to the dissimilarity factors. Our results provide guidelines for practitioners to make robust assortment decisions under distinct sources of parameter uncertainties.

title: The Voice of Fairness in Humanitarian Logistics
affiliations: , , Tsinghua University, Sheffield University Management School and School of Economics and Management, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

detail.title: The Voice of Fairness in Humanitarian Logistics
